items.title: Jim Cullum interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: The interviewee mentions Jack Teagarden only in the context of his father's career ('joined Jack Teagarden’s band') and as a source of anecdotes about other musicians (Bix Beiderbecke, Louis Armstrong). There is no evidence of a direct personal relationship between Jim Cullum and Jack Teagarden.

ctx.x: Right. Did your father make a living playing music?

He did from time to time. He went in and out of the business. At the time when I was growing up starting in 1945, that’s the last year of the war, joined Jack Teagarden’s band, and Jack Teagarden’s big band, and then left town, came back, he was coming and going with traveling bands, with another band and he came back and so we lived in Dallas at that time. But before that my first few years, which I don’t have memory of, he was working in my family’s business and playing on the side and then he became a…
Was he happy that you chose music as your career path?
